title: list -o is accepted and silently ignored
body:
`ListArgs` declares `-o/--output` (`sufr/src/lib.rs:199-201`). The `list` handler builds its `ListOptions` with `output: None` and a comment saying it defaults to stdout (`sufr/src/lib.rs:431`). The value is never read, so `sufr list -o out.txt` writes to stdout and creates no file. `ListOptions.output: Option<String>` (`libsufr/src/types.rs:469`) supports a file.

Seen by reading the code in the survey. The command was not run.

The four `*_is_sorted` tests in `sufr/tests/cli.rs` (1167-1246) use `list -o` to write a file and then check its lines are sorted. If the survey reading is right, they never see the file and may assert nothing.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4be42394
notes.text:
At cff9fb6 `list` is at `sufr/src/lib.rs:405`. Its writer is `io::stdout()` at :422, with a TODO at :421.

The four `*_is_sorted` tests (`file_is_sorted` at `cli.rs:1166`) still read a file that `list -o` never writes. The pinned test `list_output_flag_is_ignored` records the current behaviour.
